channel.description: All Things Considered hosts Ailsa Chang, Mary Louise Kelly, Juana Summers and Scott Detrow present the program's trademark mix of news, interviews, commentaries, reviews, and offbeat features 7 days a week.

item.title: Carly Rae Jepsen's new album from warm and breezy day to thumping dance floor night
item.description: Carly Rae Jepsen has now been releasing critically-acclaimed pop music for more than a decade. And Friday, she's out with her eighth album, called Day and Night.
item.content:encoded: Carly Rae Jepsen has now been releasing critically-acclaimed pop music for more than a decade. And Friday, she's out with her eighth album, called Day and Night.

item.title: Ole Miss and LSU face off in a rivalry made more bitter by Lane Kiffin's return
item.description: Lane Kiffin brings his LSU Tigers to the University of Mississippi for a highly-anticipated football game. Kiffin led Ole Miss for the past few seasons but bolted for LSU, angering many.

item.title: 'Joyful protestors' talk about the cultural value of the Kennedy Center
item.description: The center, a beacon of American arts and culture, is slated to be closed after a board vote. On Friday, a group called Hands Off the Arts is holding what they call a "joyful protest" outside.

item.title: Despite calls for Congress to take action on AI, the House went home early
item.description: In spite of growing calls for Congress to take action on AI, the House went home early and won't be back until after this November's midterm elections.

item.title: Russians head to the polls to choose lawmakers for their parliament
item.description: Russians head to the polls to choose lawmakers for their parliament, the Duma. It's Russia's first nationwide parliamentary race since launching its full scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

item.title: Overdue library magazine returned after 132 years
item.description: After the Concord Public Library in New Hampshire announced a fine freeze, a man has returned an overdue magazine published in 1894.

item.title: A new DOJ program restores ex-felons' right to own guns. What you need to know
item.description: The DOJ is making it easier for people convicted of felonies to have their gun rights restored. An estimated 330,000 people are expected to apply through the new process, which opens in mid-September.

item.title: How a pizza app changed our relationship with waiting
item.description: Status trackers are ubiquitous on online apps and ordering. We have the story the seminal Domino's Pizza Tracker that led to many copies, and we check on why many of the trackers now aren't accurate.

item.description: Rhiannon Giddens is out with a new album. For her latest project — called Hope is the Thing With Feathers — Giddens went with BIG emotions.

item.title: Nebraska voters say their income is not keeping up with their rent
item.description: When it comes to housing, what's considered affordable all depends on how much you make. This could matter in a state that is home to a key Congressional race this election season.
